title: Week in Orbit
summary: As the space sector gears up for a busy launch season, regulatory frameworks and geopolitical dynamics continue to shape the landscape. Meanwhile, funding flows and technological advancements hint at a competitive future for both commercial and defense-oriented ventures.

themes.title: Regulatory Challenges in Space
themes.body: Northern Norway's readiness for launches contrasts sharply with the EU's sluggish Arctic policy. This disconnect could hinder collaborative efforts in a region increasingly vital for strategic interests.

themes.title: China's Lunar Ambitions
themes.body: With the arrival of the Shenzhou-23 crew at Tiangong, China's lunar aspirations are becoming clearer. Their 2030 lunar landing goal is ambitious, but the timeline may face challenges as international competition heats up.

themes.title: Funding Boosts for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds a notable $1.4 billion for space resilience initiatives. This funding reflects a growing recognition of the need for robust defense capabilities in an increasingly contested space environment.

themes.title: Commercial Ventures Gain Momentum
themes.body: NASA's decision to expand its commercial crew contract with SpaceX signals confidence in private sector capabilities. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's recent funding round underscores the growing interest in innovative space solutions.
